stages.title: GAUBA'S ALLOCATIVE FRAME, RIGHTNESS AND DYNAMIC JUSTICE

pills.text: GAUBA'S ALLOCATIVE FRAME, RIGHTNESS AND DYNAMIC JUSTICE
CENTRAL FOCUS
[1] GAUBA FRAMES JUSTICE THROUGH ALLOCATIVE CONTEST UNDER SCARCITY
[2] RIGHTNESS CANNOT BE REDUCED TO AGGREGATE USEFULNESS, THOUGH
[3] DYNAMIC SOCIAL CONSCIOUSNESS EXPLAINS WHY ACCEPTED HIERARCHY CAN
[4] THE ALLOCATIVE FRAME IS NOT AN EXHAUSTIVE DEFINITION
GAUBA'S SCARCITY-OPEN SOCIETY FRAME IS ALLOCATIVE, NOT UNIVERSAL.
ANSWER USE

sequence: CENTRAL FOCUS
Gauba's Allocative Frame, Rightness and Dynamic Justice
[1] Gauba frames justice through allocative contest under scarcity and openness.
[2] Rightness cannot be reduced to aggregate usefulness, though Mill complicates a blanket anti-utilitarian claim.
[3] Dynamic social consciousness explains why accepted hierarchy can become recognised injustice.

stages.answer_line: VERDICT → Gauba's scarcity-open society frame is allocative, not universal.

stages.title: TRADITIONAL JUSTICE, SOCIAL JUSTICE AND BARKER'S ORDERING

pills.text: TRADITIONAL JUSTICE, SOCIAL JUSTICE AND BARKER'S ORDERING
CENTRAL FOCUS
[1] TRADITIONAL JUSTICE ORDERS DIFFERENTIATED ROLES; MODERN SOCIAL JUSTICE
[2] PLATO'S FUNCTIONAL HARMONY IS HIERARCHICAL BUT SHOULD NOT
[3] BARKER ORDERS LIBERTY, EQUALITY AND FRATERNITY RATHER THAN
[4] FRATERNITY CONVERTS PROTECTION OF WEAKER MEMBERS FROM CHARITY
JUSTICE ORDERS LIBERTY, EQUALITY AND FRATERNITY INTO ONE SCHEME.
ANSWER USE

sequence: CENTRAL FOCUS
Traditional Justice, Social Justice and Barker's Ordering
[1] Traditional justice orders differentiated roles; modern social justice transforms oppressive arrangements.
[2] Plato's functional harmony is hierarchical but should not be simplified into completely closed hereditary
[3] Barker orders liberty, equality and fraternity rather than listing them separately.

stages.title: LAW, LEGALITY AND THE INSTITUTIONAL DIMENSIONS OF JUSTICE

pills.text: LAW, LEGALITY AND THE INSTITUTIONAL DIMENSIONS OF JUSTICE
CENTRAL FOCUS
[1] ROSS ASKS WHETHER EXISTING LAW IS IMPARTIALLY ADMINISTERED.
[2] BARKER ASKS WHETHER LAW ITSELF POSSESSES DEFENSIBLE MORAL
[3] LEGAL, POLITICAL AND SOCIO-ECONOMIC JUSTICE TEST DIFFERENT BUT
[4] VALIDITY, DEMOCRATIC VOICE AND MATERIAL ACCESS MUST REMAIN
VALID ADMINISTRATION CANNOT SETTLE THE JUSTICE OF LEGAL CONTENT.
ANSWER USE

sequence: CENTRAL FOCUS
Law, Legality and the Institutional Dimensions of Justice
[1] Ross asks whether existing law is impartially administered.
[2] Barker asks whether law itself possesses defensible moral value.
[3] Legal, political and socio-economic justice test different but connected institutions.

stages.title: PROCEDURAL LIBERALISM, BACKGROUND INEQUALITY AND MACPHERSON

pills.text: PROCEDURAL LIBERALISM, BACKGROUND INEQUALITY AND MACPHERSON
CENTRAL FOCUS
[1] HAYEK, FRIEDMAN AND NOZICK ARE GROUPED BY GAUBA
[2] MACPHERSON SHOWS HOW BACKGROUND INEQUALITY CAN HOLLOW OUT
[3] DUE PROCESS REMAINS NECESSARY EVEN WHEN PROCEDURE IS
[4] A FAIR-LOOKING RULE IS NOT SUFFICIENT PROOF OF
PROCEDURE IS NECESSARY BUT BACKGROUND POWER CAN DEFEAT ITS
ANSWER USE

sequence: CENTRAL FOCUS
Procedural Liberalism, Background Inequality and Macpherson
[1] Hayek, Friedman and Nozick are grouped by Gauba but defend different procedural arguments.
[2] Macpherson shows how background inequality can hollow out formally voluntary competition.
[3] Due process remains necessary even when procedure is substantively incomplete.

stages.title: NOZICK, MERIT, NEED AND DESERT

pills.text: NOZICK, MERIT, NEED AND DESERT
CENTRAL FOCUS
[1] NOZICK'S THEORY IS HISTORICAL, ENTITLEMENT-BASED AND UNPATTERNED.
[2] ACQUISITION IS LIMITED BY A LOCKEAN PROVISO; UNJUST
[3] MERIT, NEED AND DESERT ANSWER DIFFERENT DISTRIBUTIVE QUESTIONS.
[4] PROGRESSIVE TAXATION CAN FINANCE A FLOOR BUT DOES
ENTITLEMENT REQUIRES ACQUISITION, TRANSFER, PROVISO AND RECTIFICATION.
ANSWER USE

sequence: CENTRAL FOCUS
Nozick, Merit, Need and Desert
[1] Nozick's theory is historical, entitlement-based and unpatterned.
[2] Acquisition is limited by a Lockean proviso; unjust history activates rectification.
[3] Merit, need and desert answer different distributive questions.

stages.title: RAWLS, SEN AND THE INFORMATION OF JUSTICE

pills.text: RAWLS, SEN AND THE INFORMATION OF JUSTICE
CENTRAL FOCUS
[1] RAWLS STATES TWO LEXICALLY ORDERED PRINCIPLES, NOT THREE
[2] FAIR EQUALITY OF OPPORTUNITY PRECEDES THE DIFFERENCE PRINCIPLE
[3] SEN SEPARATES CAPABILITY AS INFORMATIONAL SPACE FROM COMPARATIVE
[4] RAWLS, NOZICK AND SEN DISAGREE OVER PROCEDURE, OBJECT
RAWLS, NOZICK AND SEN EVALUATE DIFFERENT OBJECTS BY DIFFERENT
ANSWER USE

sequence: CENTRAL FOCUS
Rawls, Sen and the Information of Justice
[1] Rawls states two lexically ordered principles, not three independent principles.
[2] Fair equality of opportunity precedes the difference principle within the second principle.
[3] Sen separates capability as informational space from comparative, realisation-focused method.
